title: 3.8.11 Lab: Round-Trip an Array of Objects
description: Round-trip a game-state shape — an object holding an array of item objects — through stringify and parse, then read a nested field back. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build the game-state object
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it gameState; use any name that fits) holding an object with a player name and an array called items of at least two item objects. Each item should have a name and a price.

steps.title: Save the whole thing
steps.instructions: Use JSON.stringify to turn gameState into text, stored in a variable (the lesson calls it saved).

steps.title: Restore it and reach a nested field
steps.instructions: Use JSON.parse on saved to rebuild it into a new variable (the lesson calls it restored), then use console.log to print the price of the second item plus ten, and the item's name. The nesting is array inside object.

requirements.title: Game-state object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Declare an object in braces for the game state (the lesson calls it gameState).

requirements.title: Saved with stringify
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify to produce text. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: JSON.stringify(gameState) turns the whole thing into text.

requirements.title: Restored with parse
requirements.description: Calls JSON.parse on the saved text. Help: 3.8.8 (JSON.parse — Text Back to Object)
requirements.hint: JSON.parse on the saved text gives back an object you can read from.

requirements.title: Output printed
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Print the second item's price plus ten, and its name, reading from the restored object.

requirements.title: restored is rebuilt from the saved text and the second item is read
requirements.description: saved is a string, restored holds the same data as gameState, and the second item's price plus ten and its name were printed. Help: 3.8.9 (A Round Trip)
requirements.hint: saved = JSON.stringify(gameState), restored = JSON.parse(saved), then print restored.items[1].price + 10 and restored.items[1].name.

checks.expr: typeof saved === 'string' && JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(saved)) === JSON.stringify(gameState) && Array.isArray(gameState.items) && gameState.items.length >= 2 && JSON.stringify(restored) === JSON.stringify(gameState) && (J => J.includes(String(restored.items[1].price + 10)) && J.includes(String(restored.items[1].name)))(output.join(' ')) && !same('restored', 'gameState')
checks.fail: saved should be the JSON text of gameState, restored should hold the same data rebuilt from it, and you should print the second item's price plus ten and its name.

requirements.title: saved and restored come from gameState, and the second item is printed from restored
requirements.description: When gameState holds other values, saved and restored change with it, and console.log calls that run print the second item's price plus ten and its name, read from restored. Help: 3.8.9 (A Round Trip)
requirements.hint: Print restored.items[1].price + 10 and restored.items[1].name. Text typed in by hand does not change when gameState does.

checks.fail: saved has to be the text JSON.stringify makes from gameState: when the checker changes gameState, saved must change with it. Text typed in by hand stays the same.
restored has to come from JSON.parse(saved): when the checker changes gameState, restored must change with it. An object typed in by hand stays the same.
Print the second item's price plus ten from restored, console.log(restored.items[1].price + 10), with a console.log that runs. Typed-in text does not count.
Print the second item's name from restored, console.log(restored.items[1].name), with a console.log that runs.
